_comment: Named circuits worth looking at, kept as data so that the visualizer stays
generic and the biology stays reviewable. Each entry lists SEED cells; the
These groupings are conventional descriptions from the C. elegans literature.
Naming a set of cells 'the touch circuit' is a summary of many ablation and
imaging experiments, not something the connectome states. Treat each entry as
a starting point for looking, not as a claim about what the circuit does.

gentle-touch.description: Gentle body touch mechanosensory neurons and the command interneurons they drive. Anterior touch (ALM, AVM) is associated with reversal; posterior touch (PLM) with forward acceleration.
gentle-touch.source: Chalfie M, Sulston JE, White JG, Southgate E, Thomson JN, Brenner S. The neural circuit for touch sensitivity in Caenorhabditis elegans. J Neurosci 5:956-964 (1985).
gentle-touch.note: PLML/PLMR and PVM are outside the Witvliet reconstruction volume in some datasets.

nociception.description: ASH polymodal nociceptor and its immediate postsynaptic partners. ASH responds to noxious chemicals, high osmolarity and nose touch.
nociception.source: Kaplan JM, Horvitz HR. A dual mechanosensory and chemosensory neuron in Caenorhabditis elegans. PNAS 90:2227-2231 (1993).

command-interneurons.description: The premotor command interneurons associated with backward (AVA, AVD, AVE) and forward (AVB, PVC) locomotion.
command-interneurons.source: Chalfie M, et al. J Neurosci 5:956-964 (1985); Kawano T, et al. Neuron 72:572-586 (2011).
command-interneurons.note: These interneurons are present in the Witvliet datasets, but the ventral-cord motor neurons they drive are not.

salt-chemotaxis.description: ASE left/right chemosensory pair, functionally asymmetric for salt sensing, and the first interneuron layer downstream.
salt-chemotaxis.source: Pierce-Shimomura JT, Morse TM, Lockery SR. The fundamental role of pirouettes in Caenorhabditis elegans chemotaxis. J Neurosci 19:9557-9569 (1999); Suzuki H, et al. Nature 454:114-117 (2008).

odour-sensing.description: AWA, AWB and AWC olfactory neurons and their downstream interneurons.
odour-sensing.source: Bargmann CI, Hartwieg E, Horvitz HR. Odorant-selective genes and neurons mediate olfaction in C. elegans. Cell 74:515-527 (1993).

oxygen-sensing.description: URX, AQR and BAG oxygen/carbon-dioxide sensors and the RMG hub they are gap-junctioned to.
oxygen-sensing.source: Macosko EZ, et al. A hub-and-spoke circuit drives pheromone attraction and social behaviour in C. elegans. Nature 458:1171-1175 (2009).
